 Fish product sold in Pennsylvania recalled for ‘possible health risk’ 
 by: Mac Bell 
 Posted: Oct 19, 2026 / 11:21 AM EDT 
 Updated: Oct 19, 2026 / 11:21 AM EDT 
 by: Mac Bell 
 Posted: Oct 19, 2026 / 11:21 AM EDT 
 Updated: Oct 19, 2026 / 11:21 AM EDT 
 SHARE 
 (WHMT) — The U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) announced the recall of a fish product that was sold in six states, including Pennsylvania.
 According to the FDA, Krasnyi Oktyabr, Inc. of Brooklyn, New York, has recalled its Starfish Seafood Premium Cold Smoked Norwegian Salmon Sliced (UPC Code: 4751048940099) because it could be contaminated with Listeria. 
 Close

 This recalled sliced salmon product was distributed in New York, Florida, Georgia, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ohio.
 The FDA says the potential Listeria contamination was discovered after a sampling was performed by the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets.
 No illnesses have been reported in connection to this recall.
 It should be noted that Krasnyi Oktyabr Inc. is a wholesale distributor and did not manufacture the recalled product. Currently, the company has notified its affected customers and requested that they discontinue the sale and distribution of the product.
 If you purchased the recalled salmon, you should return it to the place of purchase for a full refund.
 Any questions can be directed to Kransnyi Oktyabr by calling 718-858-6720.
